description: CRA Board: staff recommends funding the Downtown Placemaking Program, not to exceed $150,000.
CRA Board: Commercial Property Improvement Program grant of $56,920 for exterior improvements at 1229 W. Tharpe Street.
Nov 13 (FOX 35): Sheriff Rick Staly proposed a dedicated law-enforcement tax (MSTU) to offset an estimated $15M shortfall next year (paraphrase).
Nov 12 (WJHG): Board to form a committee to identify cuts; draft list of 23 programs incl. animal control and libraries; about $2.7M potential revenue loss from 2028. Commissioner Sandy Quinn spoke.
Nov 9 (Jacksonville Today): CAO Mike Weinstein: "Maybe the libraries will be open not quite as long." $150M to almost $200M less next budget; $300M by FY2028-29.

Nov 13 (Tallahassee Democrat): Leon Commissioners Maddox ("our responsibility now is to govern"), Minor (deeper cuts elsewhere), O'Keefe (cuts alone cannot offset loss); Tallahassee Commissioner Williams-Cox: "significant budget challenges."
Nov 8 (LBK News): Commissioner Gary Coffin: Town anticipates about $1.4 million in reduced annual General Fund revenue.
Nov 8 (WUSF/WQCS): Commissioner Blake Capps: "These are rather severe cuts." Gap about $42M in 2027, about $75M in 2028.
Nov 11 (WKMG): Commissioner Patty Sheehan: "This is a 90 percent budget cut." Mayor Buddy Dyer: "some difficult decisions."
Nov 14 (WEAR): Mayor D.C. Reeves: "our general fund is going to be cut by 30% across the board"; park property sales on the table. Council President Allison Patton expects personnel cuts.
WEAR, Nov 14: "Pensacola mayor says selling some park properties is on the table amid Amendment 3 cuts". Notes $210,000 Dunwoody Park renovation and $21.7M park plan.
Nov 17 agenda staff memo: recommends ending city funding of Beach Trolley service, citing Amendment 3; projects ad valorem loss of about $1M in FY28 and over $2.4M in FY29.
Tallahassee Democrat, Nov 13: "Freshly elected officials face first test with Amendment 3 budget strain". Cites city executive salaries rising to $260,283.
